text: {"observations":"From 0 to about 3 s there are steady, flat harmonic stacks that step in pitch at roughly 0.6, 1.3, 1.9 and 2.6 s. The harmonics are dense and stay strong up to about 5-7 kHz for the full length of each note, with no obvious decay after the onset and no vibrato wobble. Sustained, reed-like, harmonically rich notes fit an accordion (B). A piano (A) would show partials fading quickly after each attack, especially the high ones. A violin (C) would normally show vibrato. A flute (D) would have only a few weak upper harmonics. The gliding harmonics after about 3.5 s look like a voice entering later, not the opening instrument. This is an inference from the images, not a certain identification.","answer":"B"}
